newsitem.title: UK: UK Tory leader ballot result due 1630 GMT Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: UK Tory leader ballot result due 1630 GMT Tuesday.

text.p: The result of the first ballot for the leadership of Britain's main opposition Conservative party will be announced at 1630 GMT on Tuesday.
To win outright on the first ballot, one of the five candidates must win more than 50 percent of the votes of the 164 Conservative members of parliament who make up the electorate.
In addition, he must be 15 percent ahead of the runner-up.
This makes it probable that a second ballot will be needed, which would be held on June 17.
Any Conservative MP can stand in the second ballot, including those who have not contested the first round. Nominations would have to be submitted by 1100 GMT on June 12.
To win on the second ballot, a simple majority (83 votes) is needed.
If there is no winner on June 17, the two front-runners will square off in a third and final ballot on June 19.
Voting takes place between 0900 GMT and 1600 GMT in a committee room of the House of Commons under the auspices of the 1922 committee of Conservative backbench MPs.

The result will be announced by the chairman of the committee, Sir Archie Hamilton, who intends to issue on Tuesday morning the results of a consultative ballot of Conservative constituency chairmen and Conservative MEPs.
